reviews.text: I've been going to the clinic for about two years now, for the care of my two cats, and I've always been satisfied! The rates are absolutely reasonable.

I went to the Corsica Clinic for a problem with my cat. The problem was due to an inflammation of the respiratory tract. I found a caring and thorough doctor who patiently examined my cat and explained how to treat her. I was very satisfied with the visit. Blood tests were also performed for thoroughness. I would recommend this veterinary center to all pet owners.

A transparent and honest veterinary clinic with reasonable costs compared to other veterinary clinics. I had a former stray cat, the result of a relinquishment of ownership after two years of adoption. She was about 3 years old and still feral and neglected by her former owner, who had never seen a vet in her life. She wouldn't let anyone touch her, probably due to past experiences that had traumatized her. I spoke directly with the surgeon and explained the problem: the former stray wouldn't let anyone touch her. I asked him if it was possible to do everything in a single appointment: a general examination, complete fecal analysis, FIV and FELV tests, general and preparatory tests for spaying and neutering. The surgeon understood the situation and did everything in a single morning. Then I brought the cat back to the clinic after about 10 days to remove the collar because she wouldn't let anyone touch her. The entire staff was extremely kind; they removed my cat's Elizabethan collar 10 days after her spay, even though I hadn't made an appointment for that day. The spay went well. The staff was competent, helpful, and extremely kind and empathetic toward animals. I had previously contacted and visited two other veterinary clinics, but this clinic impressed me positively not only for its expertise, honesty, and transparency regarding veterinary service costs, but also for the kindness of the staff, as well as for the permanent presence of two formerly stray cats adopted by the clinic itself. The fact that this veterinary clinic has adopted two formerly stray cats, who are now permanently resident in this clinic, which has now become their home, demonstrates that the staff cares for animals and empathizes with animal welfare, and that the work of the people who work at this clinic is driven by a passion for animals and their well-being.
Always kind and attentive in caring for my furry friends, I always make appointments with Dr. Camilla who is truly competent and helpful!

Unfortunately, I can't give a higher rating based on my experiences. My partner, Mantovani M., and my dog, Susumu, presented symptoms such as clearly visible abdominal swelling, very frequent urination, and continued to drink frequently. When we went to the clinic, we spoke with Dr. Rossi, who, after a blood test with a muzzle attached, which only further agitated my little one, concluded that the dog had a simple intestinal irritation. Given that he had barely been examined, no palpation, and no attention paid to the symptoms we had repeatedly described, the doctor decided to prescribe an antibiotic for my dog. This was to ease the strain on his liver and encourage bacterial resistance. Two days later, we returned, and I met with the only doctor in the facility who was empathetic and conscientious towards Susumu, a tall, gray-haired dog, and together we decided to have an ultrasound, which then led to further tests being carried out elsewhere. Exactly two days after Dr. Rossi's visit, we discovered not only a mast cell tumor, which is unfortunately widespread, but also the absurd presence of effusion caused by the noise. Another flaw: the person who performed the ultrasound, who wasn't the one who suggested it, was rather rude and literally yelled at my dog ​​to stay still. A chilling scene. I highly recommend focusing on the patient's well-being and care. The doctor who suggested the ultrasound is truly to be thanked; Susumu was calm with him; and he was also tactful with us, as I believe that unfortunately, tact has been lacking on the part of others, and in Dr. Rossi's case, even care and listening. I regretfully remain available for any further discussion.
